```{r setup}
# run_pipeline.R sources its modules by relative path, so chunks run from the
# project root rather than from docs/.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(here)
library(scales)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  plot.title.position = "plot"))

PAL <- c("#3B6EA5", "#C1666B", "#7FB069", "#E5A34B", "#8A7090", "#9AA5B1")

read_out <- function(f) read_csv(here(f), show_col_types = FALSE)

pilot_val <- read_out("data/final_extraction_pilot1-and-pilot2.csv")
idx1      <- read_out("data/full_sample_index.csv")
ex1       <- read_out("data/final_extraction_full-empirical-sample.csv")
idx2      <- read_out("data/pilot2_sample_index.csv")
ex2       <- read_out("data/final_extraction_pilot2-sample.csv")

# The 20 extraction columns are identical across the two frames, so the samples
# stack once each row is labelled with the frame it came from.
combined <- bind_rows(
  ex1 |> mutate(frame = "pilot-1 frame"),
  ex2 |> mutate(frame = "pilot-2 frame")
)

n_frame1 <- nrow(idx1 |> filter(article_status != "pilot2"))
n_frame2 <- nrow(idx2)
n_ex1    <- nrow(ex1)
n_ex2    <- nrow(ex2)
```

## What this is

This meta-scientific assessment asks how psychology articles report **pilot
studies**, and whether articles that report one differ from those that do not on transparency
and governance markers — journal transparency policy, funding, conflicts of
interest and preregistration. Answering that needs those markers for every
article in the sampling frame, not only for the articles a human coded.

This report documents the automated pipeline that produces them: what each
column means, how accurate it is against manual coding, and what the two samples
now contain.

The unit of analysis is the **article**, identified by DOI. Every article
contributes at most one row.

## The two samples

The project drew two sampling frames, one for each pilot round. They are
independent draws from different search strategies and overlap in a single
article, so their extraction outputs stack into one dataset.

```{r tbl-samples}
#| label: tbl-samples
#| tbl-cap: "The two sampling frames and what has been extracted from each."

tibble(
  Frame = c("Pilot-1 frame", "Pilot-2 frame"),
  `Source file` = c("full_sample.csv", "pilot2_sample.csv"),
  `Articles in frame` = c(n_frame1, n_frame2),
  `Manually coded` = c(
    sum(idx1$article_status == "pilot1"),
    sum(idx2$article_status == "pilot2-coded")),
  `Extraction rows` = c(n_ex1, n_ex2)
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Sampling frames and extraction coverage") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = c(Frame, `Source file`))
```

The two frames are filtered differently, and this matters for any analysis that
pools them:

- **Pilot-1 frame** — extraction is restricted to articles an LLM classifier
  marked as *empirical*, plus every manually coded article regardless of that
  classification. Articles classified non-empirical are in the index but carry
  no extraction row.
- **Pilot-2 frame** — extracted **unfiltered**. The classifier has run over the
  pilot-1 frame only, so no `empirical` column exists for pilot 2.

To pool the frames on comparable terms, filter the pilot-1 rows on
`empirical == "yes"` in `data/full_sample_index.csv` and accept that the
pilot-2 rows are unrestricted, or run the classifier over the pilot-2 abstracts
first.

### Coverage within each frame

```{r tbl-coverage}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Why frame articles have no extraction row."

cov1 <- idx1 |>
  filter(article_status != "pilot2") |>
  mutate(state = case_when(
    doi %in% ex1$doi                  ~ "extracted",
    is.na(tei_file)                   ~ "no TEI (PDF not converted)",
    TRUE                              ~ "excluded: not classified empirical")) |>
  count(state, name = "Pilot-1 frame")

cov2 <- idx2 |>
  mutate(state = case_when(
    doi %in% ex2$doi ~ "extracted",
    is.na(tei_file)  ~ "no TEI (PDF not converted)",
    TRUE             ~ "TEI present but no extraction row")) |>
  count(state, name = "Pilot-2 frame")

full_join(cov1, cov2, by = "state") |>
  arrange(desc(coalesce(`Pilot-1 frame`, 0L) + coalesce(`Pilot-2 frame`, 0L))) |>
  rename(Status = state) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Article status within each sampling frame") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "—")
```

## Method

### Inputs

Each article enters the pipeline as a **DOI** plus a path to a **GROBID TEI**
file — a structured XML rendering of the article PDF, with headings, sections
and back-matter marked up. TEI gives the extractors document structure, so a
funding statement can be located by its heading rather than by scanning prose.

PDF → TEI conversion runs as a GitHub Action in the companion
`pilot2_pdf_conversion` repository: the PDFs live in a Google Drive folder, a
fleet of parallel runners each convert a share of them through GROBID
0.8.2.1-full, and one job commits the result.

DOI → TEI matching is deterministic. TEI filenames carry the DOI with every
`/` flattened to `-`, and a DOI suffix can itself contain `-`, so the slashes
cannot be restored by position. Both sides are therefore compared on a key that
lower-cases the DOI and rewrites `/` as `-`.

### The four extraction modules

```{r tbl-modules}
#| label: tbl-modules
#| tbl-cap: "The extraction modules, in run order."

tibble(
  Module = c("1. DOI metadata", "2. TEI funding & COI",
             "3. Preregistration", "4. Funder → country"),
  Source = c("OpenAlex + Crossref APIs", "GROBID TEI",
             "GROBID TEI + OSF API", "Crossref Funder Registry + OpenAlex/ROR"),
  Produces = c(
    "Journal, ISSN, SJR, TOP Factor, first-author affiliation, structured funder IDs, Crossref COI text, abstract",
    "Funding statement and conflict-of-interest statement text, located by document structure",
    "Preregistration present, platform, URL; registered-report and trial-registry flags",
    "Country for every named or ID-matched funder")
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Pipeline modules") |>
  cols_width(Produces ~ px(420)) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = everything())
```

Two design choices are worth stating explicitly.

**Preregistration is gated on the registration template, not on the word.** An
OSF link alone does not count: the pipeline resolves the OSF GUID through the
OSF API and asks whether the object is a *registration* and, if so, under which
template. An OSF *project* link is recorded as such and does not set
`prereg_present`. Trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and equivalents) and
AsPredicted are detected separately, and `registration_any` is the union of
preregistration, registered report and trial registry.

**Conflict of interest is classified by negation, not by presence.** A COI
statement is first located (TEI, falling back to the Crossref deposit); a
case-insensitive negation regex then decides whether it declares *no* conflict.
No statement at all is a third, distinct category — the absence of a declaration
is a finding, not a missing value.

### Caching

Every networked lookup — OpenAlex and Crossref metadata, OSF GUIDs and
registration templates, funder ID and funder name resolution — is cached to
disk. A rerun over the same DOIs makes no network calls, and
`run_pipeline(..., use_api = FALSE)` errors rather than silently reaching the
network, which is what makes the outputs reproducible offline.

### The 20 output columns

```{r tbl-columns}
#| label: tbl-columns
#| tbl-cap: "The extraction schema. Every row of both outputs has these columns."

tibble::tribble(
  ~Column, ~Meaning,
  "doi", "Article DOI, normalised to lower case (join key)",
  "journal, issn", "Venue name and primary ISSN",
  "top_factor, sjr", "Journal transparency (TOP Factor) and Scimago (SJR) scores",
  "first_author_country", "First author's country, preferring the article-level affiliation over the author's OpenAlex profile",
  "first_author_location_full", "Institution, city, region, country for the same",
  "first_author_location_source", "Which of the two supplied the location",
  "funding_category", "funded / no funding / no statement",
  "funding_statement", "The extracted funding text (audit trail)",
  "funders", "Named funders, ||-separated",
  "funding_country", "Distinct funder countries, ||-separated",
  "coi_statement", "The extracted conflict-of-interest text (audit trail)",
  "coi_category", "conflict declared / no conflict declared / no statement",
  "prereg_present", "Whether the article reports a study preregistration",
  "prereg_platform", "OSF registration, AsPredicted, ClinicalTrials.gov, …",
  "prereg_url", "Registration link(s)",
  "is_registered_report", "Registered Report",
  "is_trial_registry", "Trial or health-registry entry",
  "registration_any", "Any of the three above"
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Output schema") |>
  cols_width(Column ~ px(220), Meaning ~ px(480)) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = everything())
```

## Validation against manual coding

Two rounds of manual coding provide the ground truth: `r sum(idx1$article_status == "pilot1")`
articles in pilot 1 and `r sum(idx2$article_status == "pilot2-coded")` in pilot 2.
Three pipeline outputs have a manual counterpart in the coding form —
`funding_category`, `coi_category` and `prereg_present`. Agreement is measured
only on articles where a coder gave an answer.

```{r validation-setup}
source(here("run_pipeline.R"))

m1 <- read.csv(here("data/inputs/2025-12-09_Codingform_PilotingAssessment_pilot.csv"),
               check.names = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
m2 <- read.csv(here("data/inputs/2026-04-03_Codingform_PilotingAssessment_pilot2.csv"),
               check.names = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

man <- bind_rows(
  tibble(doi = norm_doi(m1[["X1.2..Article.DOI"]]), pilot = "pilot 1",
         mfund   = m1[["X8.1..Does.the.article.include.a.funding.statement."]],
         mcoi    = m1[["X8.2..Does.the.article.include.a.statement.indicating.whether.there.were.any.conflicts.of.interest."]],
         mprereg = m1[["X2.2...Does.the.article.state.whether.or.not.reported.study.studies.were.preregistered."]]),
  tibble(doi = norm_doi(m2[["X1.2..Article.DOI"]]), pilot = "pilot 2",
         mfund   = m2[["X8.1..Does.the.article.include.a.funding.statement."]],
         mcoi    = m2[["X8.2..Does.the.article.include.a.statement.indicating.whether.there.were.any.conflicts.of.interest..COI.."]],
         mprereg = m2[["X2.2...According.to.what.is.stated.in.the.article..were.the.reported.study.ies..preregistered.."]])
) |>
  filter(doi != "", doi != "test") |>
  distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    man_fund   = mapply(manual_funding_category, mfund, ifelse(pilot == "pilot 1", "pilot1", "pilot2")),
    man_coi    = vapply(mcoi, manual_coi_category, character(1)),
    man_prereg = vapply(mprereg, manual_prereg, logical(1)))

val <- pilot_val |> inner_join(man, by = "doi")

acc <- function(d, auto, manual) {
  keep <- !is.na(d[[manual]]) & !is.na(d[[auto]])
  tibble(n = sum(keep), agree = sum(d[[auto]][keep] == d[[manual]][keep])) |>
    mutate(accuracy = agree / n)
}

metrics <- bind_rows(
  lapply(c("pilot 1", "pilot 2"), function(p) {
    d <- val |> filter(pilot == p)
    bind_rows(
      acc(d, "funding_category", "man_fund")   |> mutate(Field = "funding_category"),
      acc(d, "coi_category",     "man_coi")    |> mutate(Field = "coi_category"),
      acc(d, "prereg_present",   "man_prereg") |> mutate(Field = "prereg_present")
    ) |> mutate(Round = p)
  }),
  {
    d <- val
    bind_rows(
      acc(d, "funding_category", "man_fund")   |> mutate(Field = "funding_category"),
      acc(d, "coi_category",     "man_coi")    |> mutate(Field = "coi_category"),
      acc(d, "prereg_present",   "man_prereg") |> mutate(Field = "prereg_present")
    ) |> mutate(Round = "pooled")
  })
```

```{r tbl-accuracy}
#| label: tbl-accuracy
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement with manual coding, on articles a coder answered."

metrics |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f (%d/%d)", accuracy, agree, n)) |>
  select(Field, Round, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Round, values_from = cell) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Accuracy against manual coding") |>
  cols_align("left", columns = Field)
```

### What a blank funding field means

The pilot-1 coding form asked for the funding statement as **free text**. Coders
filled it in when funding existed and left it empty otherwise, so a blank cannot
separate *the article has no funding statement* from *the coder did not
transcribe one*. Blanks are therefore treated as uncoded and excluded from the
funding comparison.

```{r blank-evidence}
mc <- read_out("data/cache/pipeline_metadata_cache.csv") |>
  mutate(doi = norm_doi(doi)) |>
  select(doi, funding_funder_ids_crossref)

blank1 <- val |>
  filter(pilot == "pilot 1", is.na(mfund) | trimws(mfund) == "") |>
  left_join(mc, by = "doi")

n_blank      <- nrow(blank1)
n_blank_fund <- sum(blank1$funding_category == "funded", na.rm = TRUE)
bf <- blank1 |> filter(funding_category == "funded")
n_blank_tei  <- sum(!is.na(bf$funding_statement) & nzchar(bf$funding_statement))
n_blank_xref <- sum(!is.na(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref) &
                      nzchar(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref))
n_blank_none <- sum((is.na(bf$funding_statement) | !nzchar(bf$funding_statement)) &
                      (is.na(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref) |
                         !nzchar(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref)))
n_answered1  <- sum(val$pilot == "pilot 1" & !is.na(val$mfund) & trimws(val$mfund) != "")
```

Of the **`r n_blank`** pilot-1 articles with a blank funding field, the pipeline
finds funding for **`r n_blank_fund`**. Of those, **`r n_blank_tei`** have a
funding statement in the article's own TEI and **`r n_blank_xref`** carry a
publisher-deposited Crossref funder ID — the publisher's structured record of
who paid for the work. Exactly **`r n_blank_none`** have neither. Only
**`r n_answered1`** pilot-1 articles carry an answer in the field.

Pilot 2 replaced the free-text box with a categorical question with forced
options, so its blanks are genuinely unanswered rows and every answered row
counts.

### Where the pipeline and the coders disagree

```{r tbl-confusion}
#| label: tbl-confusion
#| tbl-cap: "Pooled confusion matrices. Rows are the pipeline, columns the coder."
#| results: asis

conf_gt <- function(auto, manual, title) {
  d <- val |> filter(!is.na(.data[[manual]]), !is.na(.data[[auto]]))
  table(pipeline = d[[auto]], coder = d[[manual]]) |>
    as.data.frame.matrix() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Pipeline") |>
    gt() |>
    tab_header(title = title) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Manual coding", columns = -Pipeline) |>
    cols_align("left", columns = Pipeline)
}
```

### A known blind spot in conflict-of-interest capture

`coi_category == "no statement"` should be read with care for some publishers.
Across both frames, 62.6% of articles carry a COI statement, but the rate by
publisher runs from **13.4% for APA (`10.1037`, n = 1,036)** to **95.7% for
MDPI**, with SAGE, Springer and Taylor & Francis all between 88% and 96%. That
spread is too wide to be reporting culture alone.

Checking the source confirms it is a parsing limit. In the validation set,
detection sensitivity is **92.9% outside APA and Cambridge but 50.0% within**
(n = 27). Taking one verified case,
[10.1037/xap0000495](https://doi.org/10.1037/xap0000495): the PDF's author note
reads "The authors have no conflicts of interest to disclose", and the 87,342-character
GROBID TEI contains no match for conflict, competing interest, disclose or
disclosure at all. APA places disclosures in the page-1 author note, and GROBID
does not carry that note into the TEI. In a sample of 400 articles marked
`no statement`, only 10.2% contain any COI wording in their TEI — so the
absence is genuine for most, but not for the affected publishers.

Funding is not affected in the same way, because Crossref supplies structured
funder IDs for 58.8% of APA articles and the pipeline uses them. There is no
equivalent deposit for COI: a Crossref COI field exists for 7–9% of articles
overall and rescued none.

**Implication.** For APA, Cambridge and `10.1192` — about 1,840 articles, 21% of
the pooled dataset — `no statement` conflates "the article has none" with "we
could not see it", and treating it as an affirmative absence will produce a
spurious publisher effect.

**What is being done.** This is
[metacheck issue #325](https://github.com/scienceverse/metacheck/issues/325).
The maintainers expect it to be resolved by the forthcoming **bibr** import —
bibr is the PDF-to-JSON extraction service replacing GROBID inside metacheck,
and its author reports that it "has a section classification module that detects
ethics/funding/coi sections very well". We are seeking access to test that
claim against this set, which is a good benchmark for it: 8,711 PDFs, 345
manually coded articles, publisher-level sensitivity measured, and 12 confirmed
misses to check. bibr is not yet publicly released — there is no public
repository, image or self-hosting documentation — so the test waits on either an
API key or the server image. Until then the COI column stands as described, and
the affected publishers should be handled explicitly in any analysis.

### Every disagreement, article by article

The matrices above say how many cells disagree, not who was right. The table
below lists **every** disagreeing article so that each one can be adjudicated
against the source: what the pipeline said, what the coder said, the coder's
raw answer, and the evidence the pipeline acted on. Follow the DOI to check.

```{r disagreements}
ev_trunc <- function(x, n = 160) {
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", x)
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(x), "(nothing extracted)",
         ifelse(nchar(x) > n, paste0(substr(x, 1, n), "…"), x))
}

disagree <- bind_rows(
  val |> filter(!is.na(man_fund), funding_category != man_fund) |>
    transmute(Field = "funding_category", doi, Round = pilot,
              Pipeline = funding_category, Coder = man_fund,
              `Coder's raw answer` = ev_trunc(mfund),
              `Pipeline evidence` = ev_trunc(coalesce(funding_statement, funders))),
  val |> filter(!is.na(man_coi), coi_category != man_coi) |>
    transmute(Field = "coi_category", doi, Round = pilot,
              Pipeline = coi_category, Coder = man_coi,
              `Coder's raw answer` = ev_trunc(mcoi),
              `Pipeline evidence` = ev_trunc(coi_statement)),
  val |> filter(!is.na(man_prereg), prereg_present != man_prereg) |>
    transmute(Field = "prereg_present", doi, Round = pilot,
              Pipeline = as.character(prereg_present), Coder = as.character(man_prereg),
              `Coder's raw answer` = ev_trunc(mprereg),
              `Pipeline evidence` = ev_trunc(paste0(
                coalesce(prereg_platform, "no platform"), " — ",
                coalesce(prereg_url, "no URL"),
                ifelse(is_trial_registry, " [trial registry]", ""),
                ifelse(registration_any, " [registration_any = TRUE]", ""))))
) |> arrange(Field, Pipeline, Coder)

dis_tbl <- function(f) {
  disagree |>
    filter(Field == f) |>
    mutate(DOI = sprintf("[%s](https://doi.org/%s)", doi, doi)) |>
    select(DOI, Round, Pipeline, Coder, `Coder's raw answer`, `Pipeline evidence`) |>
    gt() |>
    fmt_markdown(columns = DOI) |>
    tab_header(title = paste(f, "— every disagreeing article"),
               subtitle = sprintf("%d of %d coded articles",
                                  sum(disagree$Field == f),
                                  sum(!is.na(val[[c(funding_category = "man_fund",
                                                    coi_category = "man_coi",
                                                    prereg_present = "man_prereg")[[f]]]])))) |>
    cols_width(DOI ~ px(230), Round ~ px(70), Pipeline ~ px(120), Coder ~ px(120),
               `Coder's raw answer` ~ px(240), `Pipeline evidence` ~ px(360)) |>
    tab_options(table.width = pct(100), table.font.size = px(13)) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(size = px(12)),
              locations = cells_body(columns = c(`Coder's raw answer`, `Pipeline evidence`))) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(whitespace = "nowrap"),
              locations = cells_body(columns = c(DOI, Round, Pipeline, Coder))) |>
    cols_align("left", columns = everything())
}
```

```{r dis-download}
#| results: asis
csv <- paste(capture.output(write.csv(disagree, row.names = FALSE)), collapse = "\n")
cat(sprintf(
  '<p><a download="pipeline_coder_disagreements.csv" href="data:text/csv;base64,%s">Download all %d disagreements as CSV</a> — for adjudicating offline and recording a verdict per row.</p>',
  base64enc::base64encode(charToRaw(csv)), nrow(disagree)))
```

**One pattern to check first.** Several preregistration disagreements look
definitional rather than factual: the pipeline separates a *preregistration*
from a *trial-registry* entry, so an article registered on ClinicalTrials.gov
gets `prereg_present = FALSE` but `registration_any = TRUE`, while a coder
asked "were the studies preregistered?" may reasonably answer yes. Where the
evidence column shows `[trial registry]`, the two are answering different
questions, and `registration_any` is the column that matches the coder's
intent.

## Results

All figures below come from the two extraction outputs as they stand:
`r comma(n_ex1)` articles from the pilot-1 frame and `r comma(n_ex2)` from the
pilot-2 frame. Read differences *between* frames with care — the pilot-1 rows
are restricted to articles classified empirical, the pilot-2 rows are not, and
the two frames were drawn by different search strategies. The comparison the
study is designed to make is *within* the pilot-2 frame, between keyword hits
and non-hits.

```{r results-setup}
share <- function(d, col) {
  d |> count(frame, value = .data[[col]]) |>
    group_by(frame) |> mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup()
}

fund_share   <- share(combined, "funding_category")
coi_share    <- share(combined, "coi_category")
reg_share    <- combined |>
  count(frame, value = registration_any) |>
  group_by(frame) |> mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(value = ifelse(value, "registered", "not registered"))

pct <- function(d, v, f) {
  x <- d |> filter(frame == f, value == v)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return("0%")
  sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x$pct)
}
```

### Funding, conflicts of interest and registration

```{r fig-categories}
#| label: fig-categories
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the three headline categories across the two frames."
#| fig-height: 6

bind_rows(
  fund_share |> mutate(field = "Funding"),
  coi_share  |> mutate(field = "Conflict of interest"),
  reg_share  |> mutate(field = "Any registration")
) |>
  mutate(field = factor(field, c("Funding", "Conflict of interest", "Any registration"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, value, fill = frame)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.65) +
  facet_wrap(~field, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL[1:2]) +
  labs(x = "Share of extracted articles", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

```{r tbl-headline}
#| label: tbl-headline
#| tbl-cap: "Headline shares by frame."

bind_rows(
  fund_share |> mutate(Field = "funding_category"),
  coi_share  |> mutate(Field = "coi_category"),
  reg_share  |> mutate(Field = "registration_any")
) |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", comma(n), 100 * pct)) |>
  select(Field, Category = value, frame, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = frame, values_from = cell) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Field") |>
  tab_header(title = "Funding, COI and registration by frame") |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  cols_align("left", columns = Category)
```

Three things stand out.

**Funding statements are far more common in the pilot-1 frame** —
`r pct(fund_share, "funded", "pilot-1 frame")` of its articles are recorded as
funded against `r pct(fund_share, "funded", "pilot-2 frame")` in the pilot-2
frame — and the gap runs the other way for articles with no funding statement at
all. The frames' journal mixes differ enough to explain this without any
pipeline difference: the TOP Factor is missing for
`r comma(sum(is.na(ex2$top_factor)))` pilot-2 articles against
`r comma(sum(is.na(ex1$top_factor)))` in pilot 1, meaning the pilot-2 frame
reaches further outside the set of journals with a recorded transparency policy.

**Conflict-of-interest reporting goes the other way.** A COI statement of some
kind is present for `r sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * mean(ex2$coi_category != "no statement"))`
of pilot-2 articles against `r sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * mean(ex1$coi_category != "no statement"))`
of pilot-1 articles. Declared conflicts remain rare in both
(`r pct(coi_share, "conflict declared", "pilot-1 frame")` and
`r pct(coi_share, "conflict declared", "pilot-2 frame")`); the common case by
far is an explicit statement that there is no conflict.

**Registration is a minority practice in both frames** —
`r pct(reg_share, "registered", "pilot-1 frame")` and
`r pct(reg_share, "registered", "pilot-2 frame")` of articles report any
registration at all.

### Preregistration platforms

```{r fig-platforms}
#| label: fig-platforms
#| fig-cap: "Where articles that report a registration register it."

combined |>
  filter(!is.na(prereg_platform)) |>
  tidyr::separate_rows(prereg_platform, sep = "\\|\\|") |>
  mutate(prereg_platform = trimws(prereg_platform)) |>
  count(frame, prereg_platform) |>
  group_by(prereg_platform) |> filter(sum(n) >= 5) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(prereg_platform = reorder(prereg_platform, n, sum)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, prereg_platform, fill = frame)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.65) +

```

### Pilot-keyword screening

The pilot-2 index records whether the pilot-keyword screen (`pilot`,
`preliminary study`, `feasibility study`) matched anywhere outside the reference
list. This is the contrast the study is built around, and it only became
available once the whole frame was converted: the PDFs converted first were
themselves a keyword-selected subset, so the non-hit group did not exist as
machine-readable text until now.

A keyword hit is a **screen, not a coding decision** — an article that mentions a
pilot study someone else ran counts as a hit. Treat the contrast below as an
upper bound on how cleanly the groups separate.

```{r kw-setup}
kw <- ex2 |>
  left_join(idx2 |> select(doi, keyword_hit), by = "doi") |>
  filter(!is.na(keyword_hit))

kw_test <- function(flag, label) {
  d <- kw |> mutate(y = flag)
  t <- table(d$keyword_hit, d$y)
  p <- prop.test(t[, "TRUE"], rowSums(t))
  tibble(
    Marker    = label,
    `No hit`  = p$estimate[[1]],
    `Hit`     = p$estimate[[2]],
    `Difference (pp)` = 100 * (p$estimate[[2]] - p$estimate[[1]]),
    `95% CI`  = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", -100 * p$conf.int[2], -100 * p$conf.int[1]),
    p.value   = p$p.value)
}

kw_tbl <- bind_rows(
  kw_test(kw$funding_category == "funded",  "Funded"),
  kw_test(kw$coi_category != "no statement", "COI statement present"),
  kw_test(kw$prereg_present,                "Preregistration reported"),
  kw_test(kw$registration_any,              "Any registration"))
```

```{r tbl-keyword}
#| label: tbl-keyword
#| tbl-cap: "Transparency markers by pilot-keyword screen, pilot-2 frame."

kw_tbl |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Pilot-keyword hits vs non-hits",
    subtitle = sprintf("%s hits, %s non-hits",
                       comma(sum(kw$keyword_hit)), comma(sum(!kw$keyword_hit)))) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = c(`No hit`, Hit), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Difference (pp)`, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = p.value, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = Marker)
```

```{r kw-vals}
#| echo: false
kwv <- function(m, col) kw_tbl[[col]][kw_tbl$Marker == m]
kwp <- function(m, col) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * kwv(m, col))
kwd <- function(m) sprintf("%.1f pp (95%% CI %s)", kwv(m, "Difference (pp)"), kwv(m, "95% CI"))
```

Articles the screen flags are markedly more likely to report a registration.
Any registration rises from `r kwp("Any registration", "No hit")` among non-hits
to `r kwp("Any registration", "Hit")` among hits — a difference of
`r kwd("Any registration")` — and preregistration specifically from
`r kwp("Preregistration reported", "No hit")` to
`r kwp("Preregistration reported", "Hit")`,
`r kwd("Preregistration reported")`. Funding follows the same direction more
weakly, `r kwd("Funded")`.

Conflict-of-interest reporting does not separate the groups: the difference is
`r kwd("COI statement present")`, an interval that includes zero.

Whether this reflects something about pilot studies or about the kind of
research that mentions them is not something the screen can settle — it is a
description of the frame, not a causal claim, and the manual coding is what will
distinguish articles that *report* a pilot study from those that merely mention
one.

```{r fig-keyword}
#| label: fig-keyword
#| fig-cap: "Transparency markers among pilot-keyword hits and non-hits."

kw_tbl |>
  select(Marker, `No hit`, Hit) |>
  pivot_longer(-Marker, names_to = "group", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(Marker = factor(Marker, rev(kw_tbl$Marker))) |>
  ggplot(aes(p, Marker, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`No hit` = PAL[6], Hit = PAL[1])) +
  labs(x = "Share of articles", y = NULL, fill = "Keyword screen")
```

## Reproducing this

```{r reproduce}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat("```\n",
    "# pilot-1 frame\n",
    "Rscript run_full_sample.R\n\n",
    "# pilot-2 frame\n",
    "Rscript run_pilot2_sample.R\n\n",
    "# validation against the manual coding\n",
    "PIPELINE_RUN=1 Rscript run_pipeline.R\n",
    "```\n", sep = "")
```

All three read from the on-disk caches under `data/cache/`, so a rerun makes no
network calls. Column-by-column derivation rules are in
`docs/README_pipeline.md`.

```{r session}
#| code-fold: true
sessionInfo()
```
